newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to refinance $4.047 bln in debt in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to refinance $4.047 bln in debt in 1997.

text.p: Mexico will refinance $4.047 billion in debt in 1997 through new placements in international capital markets, the Finance Ministry said Friday.
"It is important to point out that the amount mentioned above is considerably less than the corresponding placements in 1995 and 1996," the ministry said.
In a statement, the government explained the placements sought to refinance in part of the maturing debt next year which amounts to a total of $9.0339 billion.
The remaining $4.987 billion will be refinanced with funds from the InterAmerican Development Bank, the World Bank and other bilateral support credits held with foreign institutions, it added.
"In all these cases, there are commitments with the respective institutions that assure the availability of the funds," the ministry added.
In 1995, Mexico's maturing debts amounted to $33.259 billion, including the dollar-linked securities known as Tesobonos, while in 1996 the figure was $5.268 billion.
